questions.q: What is the basic composition of a ketogenic diet?
a: High fat and low carbohydrate
High protein and low fat
Low fat and high carbohydrate
Equal parts fat, protein and carbs
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines keto as a high-fat, low-carb way of eating.

a: Molecules that cells can use as an alternative fuel
Hormones that store sugar in the liver
Enzymes that break down dietary protein
Fibers that slow down digestion
questions.why: Lesson 1 says burning fat produces ketones for cells to use as fuel.

questions.q: Why can keto reduce hunger, according to the summary?
a: Fewer carbs means less insulin and fewer glucose swings
It removes all fat stored in the body
It speeds up the digestive tract considerably
It replaces meals with nutritional supplements
questions.why: Lesson 1 links lower insulin to steadier glucose and less hunger.

questions.q: What is the key to sticking to keto?
a: Planning meals ahead so you do not eat too many carbs
Skipping breakfast every single day
Eating only at restaurants you trust
Counting calories without watching carbs
questions.why: Lesson 2 says preparation and keeping tempting carbs out of the house matter most.

a: Five days of strict keto, then two days with more carbs
Alternating one week on keto with one week off
Fasting every other day with no carbs at all
Eating carbs only on weekends and fasting weekdays
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes the 70/20/10 split for five days and carbs on two.
